title: First-line drafting for internal IT support tickets
problem: Our internal IT support team spends a large share of each day answering the same routine questions about password resets, VPN access and software installs. Agents retype similar answers dozens of times a day.
current_process: Agents read each ticket in the helpdesk tool and type a reply by hand, using a knowledge base they open in a separate tab.
desired_outcome: Draft a suggested first reply for common ticket types that an agent reviews and edits before sending, so agents spend less time on repetitive typing.
data_required: Historical resolved tickets and knowledge-base articles (internal, non-sensitive)
supporting_evidence: We measured that roughly 60 percent of tickets last quarter fell into eight repeatable categories, based on a review of 400 tickets. Two senior agents confirmed the pattern.

title: Automated exam proctoring with facial recognition
problem: Some learners may attempt to cheat during online exams and we currently cannot detect it at scale.
current_process: Human invigilators watch a small sample of exams live over video.
desired_outcome: Use webcam facial recognition to monitor every learner during exams and automatically flag or block anyone the system judges to be cheating.
data_required: Live webcam video of learners, facial biometric data
supporting_evidence: A product manager believes this would reduce cheating. No baseline measurement of current cheating rates is available.

title: Use AI to improve engagement
problem: Engagement is not where we want it to be and we think AI could help.

title: Summarise recurring themes in customer support conversations
problem: Support agents notice the same product confusions coming up repeatedly, but we have no systematic way to spot which help articles need updating.
current_process: A team lead skims a sample of tickets each month and makes ad hoc notes.
desired_outcome: Produce a monthly summary of the most common recurring themes in support conversations so the content team knows which help articles to update first.
affected_user: Support team leads and help-content authors
supporting_evidence: A three-month manual review found five recurring themes, but coverage was partial and the sampling was not consistent.

title: Auto-generate the weekly internal newsletter intro
problem: Writing a short light-hearted intro paragraph for the weekly internal newsletter takes the comms coordinator about 20 minutes each week.
current_process: The coordinator writes the intro by hand each Friday.
desired_outcome: Generate a draft intro paragraph each week that the coordinator can lightly edit.
supporting_evidence: One coordinator mentioned it would be a nice-to-have. Time saving is small and affects one person.
